Maya: Heads-up — noticed p95 on /v1/generate dropped ~20ms after yesterday's routing tweak but p99 actually rose. dashboard looks inconsistent. anyone else seeing this?
Chris: saw it in the alert runbook, opened a quick check. p95 down, p99 up = suspicious. could be aggregation mismatch.
Li: routing change you mean the host-split by customer-tier? that changed which backend pool serves small payloads.
Maya: yep that one.
Olivia: can you paste the dashboard queries? might be sampling/rollup issue.
Chris: main widget is using our rollup metric `latency_ms_percentile` which is pre-aggregated by 1m buckets and then we do `max` of p95 across hosts. query looks like: `SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) FROM rollups WHERE route='/v1/generate'`
Li: hmm we compute rollups per `route_key` but routing change introduced `route_key` variants (route_key + tier). dashboards are grouping by `route` only and then merging sketches client-side. merging logic uses tdigest merge but the rollups ingestion also does a second-tier quantile compaction. double-quantizing can push tails weirdly.
Maya: so the p95 could be more stable because tail mass redistributed, while p99 is sensitive to rare high-latency shards.
Zane: timeline: routing switch at 03:12 UTC, rollout 30%->100% over 20m. telemetry shows a small spike in 03:15-03:22. I have the sampling rates too — older rollups were sampled 1/100, new pool sampled 1/10 during rollout due to debug flags.
Chris: ah sampling difference is huge. if new pool has higher sampling of slow requests we'll bias p99 upward when we merge. p95 less so.
Olivia: also check retention windows — the p99 widget uses 5m rollup->1h view, p95 uses 1m rollup->15m view. not identical.
Li: proposed fixes: (1) normalize sampling weight at ingest (store sample_weight), (2) store raw tdigest per pool and merge deterministically in dashboard, (3) add explicit `percentile_rollup` pipeline that computes global percentiles from per-host sketches, not from precomputed percentiles.
Maya: which is lowest-effort to get correct numbers quickly?
Chris: short term: make dashboard merge per-pool tdigest (we already ingest sketches), change query to `tdigest_merge(sketches)` and then `tdigest_quantile(merged, 0.99)`. that'll avoid double-quantize.
Li: I can update the dashboard query and add a transient annotation. medium term: telemetry ingestion should persist `sample_weight` and a normalized histogram, that takes more infra work.
Zane: I'll add an alert suppression for the p95 anomaly window and annotate the change in the rollout timeline.
telemetry-bot: Note: rollout id r-2025-11-03-42 by @Li triggered at 03:12 UTC.
Maya: thanks. Chris, Li — can you pair and push a dashboard PR? put steps in the PR description: query change, example `SELECT tdigest_quantile(tdigest_merge(sketches), 0.99) AS p99 FROM telemetry WHERE route_key LIKE '/v1/generate%'` and a note about sampling differences.
Chris: will do. assigning to me + Li. target to ship in 2h.
Li: will also add a unit test around sketch merge semantics (edge case: tiny-weight sketches).
Olivia: once PR up I can validate against raw logs and run an offline job: `python tools/percentile_check.py --route /v1/generate --window 2025-11-03T03:00:00Z/2025-11-03T04:00:00Z` to compare.
Maya: sweet. Zane, leave the incident note in the changelog.
Zane: done, added note and muted the noisy alert. :white_check_mark:
Chris: PR link: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/dashboards/pulls/482 (draft)
Li: updated query and added comment about sample_weight.
Maya: great. we'll re-open alerts if the corrected p99 still spikes after normalizing. thanks everyone. :rocket:
